quirks.condition: An accepted F on an item that has now failed fewer than three times.
quirks.effect: The item re-enters the queue at its original priority minus 10 per failure accumulated so far, floored at 1; the per-item failure count persists across the session and is never printed.

quirks.condition: An item re-entering the queue after an accepted F, versus an item re-entering through K.
quirks.effect: A requeued item keeps its original arrival sequence number, so among equal priorities it dequeues ahead of any item enqueued after its first arrival; an item drained by K receives a fresh sequence number and goes behind everything already waiting at its priority.

quirks.condition: An accepted F whose computed requeue priority is an exact multiple of 100.
quirks.effect: The item is dead-lettered immediately with a DLQ reply, whatever its failure count.

quirks.condition: An accepted F on an item whose original priority is 999.
quirks.effect: The requeue priority is computed from a base of 1000, so the first requeue lands at 990 and the second at 980, with the result clamped to the range 1 to 999.

quirks.condition: An F naming the second most recently dequeued item, when the most recently dequeued item has already been failed and the named item has not.
quirks.effect: The F is accepted and processed as a normal failure; the engine remembers the last two dequeues, not only the most recent one.

quirks.condition: An item id that differs only in letter case from one already seen in the session.
quirks.effect: It is treated as the same item for enqueue, fail, and dead-letter state, and output lines echo the first-seen spelling.

quirks.condition: An N, D, F, or K command carrying more tokens than documented.
quirks.effect: The extra tokens are ignored and the command runs normally; FMT rejects echo the item token, or ???????? when it is missing or malformed.

unmapped_families.reason: Two mixed 150+ command corpora exercising every quirk above together with the documented behaviour; no single quirk maps.

reader_questions.question: An item is enqueued at priority 110, then dequeued, then reported failed with F. Input ends there. What is the fourth number on the X trailer line?
reader_questions.verification:
printf 'N q 110
D
F q
' | .venv/bin/python builder/gold_queuecore.py -> OK 1 / I q / DLQ q / X 1 1 1 1

reader_questions.question: An item is enqueued at priority 999, then dequeued, then reported failed with F once. At what priority does it wait in the queue after that F?
reader_questions.verification:
printf 'N a 999
N c 990
D
F a
D
D
' | .venv/bin/python builder/gold_queuecore.py -> OK 1 / OK 2 / I a / OK 2 / I a / I c / X 2 3 1 0. Item a dequeues ahead of c, which waits at 990 with a later sequence number, so a rejoined at exactly 990 (at 989 the order would be c then a).
